title: Shared work follows the reviewer

slide.title: An interactive caller promotes the retained work scope
slide.narrative:
- An interactive caller can promote an existing shared operation without replacing it. Each shared GitHub read joins the retained work before attaching its reader.
- The operation retains its scope across awaits. Child work keeps a parent link, so later requests can inherit the promotion.
- The client gives the scheduler a scope object, not a fixed priority. The scheduler reads its effective priority when it selects pending work.
- Active requests continue. Parallel execution also requires the task's parallel flag; other work remains exclusive. The client handles pacing outside the scheduler's selection rule.

fileSummaries.summary: Retained work scopes connect caller promotion to pending selection and priority inheritance.
One operation supplies a shared promise to attached readers.
Client work supplies its scope to the scheduler and waits outside the slot between paced attempts.

inlineExplanations.text: `createSharedRead` starts the operation during construction, so `work` exists before a caller uses `read`. Joining promotes that same work; it does not start another operation.
A user caller can clear the automatic classification even at equal priority. Priority promotion and automatic allowance classification are separate parts of the join.
Promotion can satisfy the priority condition, but it cannot add parallel permission. The task retains the parallel flag supplied when it entered the queue.
The scheduled attempt has returned `paced` before this wait starts. Its slot is released, and the next attempt submits the retained scope again.

svgIllustration.title: Promotion follows retained scope links
svgIllustration.takeaway: The caller changes existing work. Pending selection and later child work read the retained priority.
svgIllustration.assumptions: The illustration shows an existing foreground shared operation joined by an interactive caller. Connections show responsibilities, not elapsed time. Cancellation and allowance accounting are omitted.

entities.label: Shared GitHub work
entities.summary: Retains one GitHubWork and joins it before attaching each reader.

entities.label: Client request work
entities.summary: Runs scheduling attempts inside a retained scope and waits outside the slot after a paced result.

entities.label: Scheduler
entities.summary: Selects pending work by effective priority and controls exclusive or permitted parallel execution.

relationships.label: Raise retained priority
relationships.summary: A higher-priority caller updates the existing work scope.

relationships.label: Inherit parent priority
relationships.summary: Child work retains the current scope as its parent; effective priority includes higher parent priorities.

relationships.label: Submit scope
relationships.summary: Each scheduling attempt supplies githubPriorityScope() and the read parallel permission.

relationships.label: Read effective priority
relationships.summary: Pending selection reads the retained scope and its parent priorities rather than a copied priority value.

plan.question: How does a caller promotion reach pending and later requests without replacing the shared operation?
plan.visualApproach: Use a static behavior map with retained shared work above child request work. Put the caller beside the shared work and the scheduler below the child. Show priority inheritance separately from submission and selection.
plan.whyThisForm: The important relationship is a retained scope link, not a sequence of queue values. The map keeps the same operation visible and separates pending selection from active execution.
plan.encodings: Boxes identify responsibilities. The shared work border marks the scope that the caller updates. Upward arrows show parent-priority lookup. Downward arrows show request submission. A separate active region marks requests that promotion does not interrupt.
plan.motion: Static by design. Persistent scope links explain both pending and later requests without implying that scope updates preempt active execution.
plan.prediction: A child request created after an await can use interactive priority through its parent link, while an already active request continues.
plan.restingState: The caller update, retained parent link, scheduler scope read, and active-request boundary remain visible together.

scenarios.title: One operation, shared priority
scenarios.input: An interactive caller joins existing foreground work.

frames.title: The scheduler reads retained scopes
frames.caption: The scope can change while work waits. Selection reads its current effective priority; active execution is not interrupted.
